source_scope: Only the assigned source image, anonymous box list, generic blind rules, and generated crop manifest/crops were read. No witnesses, first TSV, draft, page, reports, notes, hand log, candidate readings or comparison were accessed.
general: The page revises a verbal description of inertia/decomposition notation into formulas, discusses a composite and a local section interpretation, and turns to a divisor and a numerical parameter. All 23 anonymous boxes were read visually. No proof, mathematical equivalence, identity or numerical claim was checked. Doubts remain on heavily cancelled words, the small connector heads and eta/u-shaped indices, one possible cancellation of que, local accents and the crowded initial transition word.

box_notes.note: The live I has a low s and a separate prime. The relation has a wavy upper stroke and a straight lower stroke. The raised E with tilde K is attached by a curved leader after the relation, replacing the cancelled verbal phrase est le groupe. The q/g-shaped descender in groupe and the final low p/e traces remain visible through the strike. The partially included dark page number above is handled separately in B021.

There are two separate wavy marks, one above the other, over a sharp K. Both are retained as nested tildes. The K has a long upright, upper oblique branch and detached-looking lower right branch; no old cancelled letter is inferred from its retracing.

The live right word is strict, followed by a closing parenthesis. To its left, diagonal hatching covers a short lower word tentatively read pas, with non as an alternative. The low p-like loop, middle angular bowl and final small curve favor pas, but the crossing is heavy. A second cancelled group above the opening-parenthesis area resembles ou; it is represented as a raised insertion subsequently cancelled. The opening parenthesis is retained. Clipped upper ordinary-text fragments are excluded.

N has low s and a separate prime. A long cancellation crosses est celui, a short qui/du-like word, and correspond. The latter has a low p descender followed by a final d ascender, supporting correspond as one word. The raised replacement reads s'identifie de, then two short horizontal bars, then à. The bars are preserved literally as = and are not expanded into a word. The replacement is placed after N_s prime at the old phrase location.
hensélisé has visible accent-like marks in the appropriate upper positions, followed by pas strict and a large closing parenthesis. There is no detached hyphen or stop to add.

The cancelled small word favors de: a looped d with a tall stem is followed by a long low e-like return. Several oblique strokes cross the first letter and connect into the cancellation. No replacement word is supplied.

Complete composite formula retained as doubtful. K in the first term is angular and capital. The middle term has a large U followed by a smaller low eta/u-shaped glyph, and the final E has a similarly shaped low glyph. No tildes are isolated in these indices. Each connector ends with a small dark angled turn, favoring an arrowhead but not excluding a bare shaft; both local alternatives are retained. No map or index is normalized from expected mathematics.

The raised parenthetical insertion reads (a priori, il envoie I_s prime dans T). The opening curved stroke, comma after priori, low prime on s and final closing parenthesis are retained. It lies between the composite formula and the following ordinary baseline. The lower clipped Ce qui... context is not duplicated.
The cancelled word favors pour. Its initial p-like descending curve, low round o bowl and following flattened u/r traces remain under a long strike. No terminal point is distinct.

The first word is que. Its thick connecting line could be normal cursive connection, and no securely separate extending cancellation stroke is visible; live que is therefore preferred, with deleted que retained as a state alternative. The formula has small s prime, membership, and capital S prime. The following short mark plus longer low joined marks are tentatively treated as suspension points; the complete formula is marked doubtful. A large closing parenthesis is live.

The source has the three separate written words que un hom. The first que has a long q descender and remaining low u/e strokes; no apostrophe is present to support an elided qu'un. hom has no detached abbreviation stop.

The first index resembles k(s), with K(s) retained as a case alternative. The first map has a strong, unmistakable right-pointing head. The middle term has U with nested round O, a wavy mark over O and a low s; no independent underline under O is apparent. The next connector has a left-pointing head and a wavy mark above its shaft, represented by a left arrow labelled sim. The final term is E_X_s. The separate final comma is retained. No equivalence was checked.

The live words are qui and the line-end fragment s'inter. The cancelled short word favors peut, from a p descender, low e-like bowl, rising u and final t-like stroke; passe remains an alternative under the crossing. Raised donc is linked by a curved leader into the gap before s'inter, after the cancelled word. No line-end hyphen is visible or supplied. Clipped upper-line descenders are excluded.

The next-line fragment is prete/prète, followed by comme. The t has a large tall peak and a cross stroke, while no distinct detached grave over the preceding low e can be securely separated; the unaccented spelling is preferred locally, with prète retained. This continues the s'inter fragment in B013. No punctuation is added.

The cancelled initial word favors Ainsi, with Aussi as an alternative because its capital and first short letters are densely crossed. The hatching is concentrated over the beginning; the remaining n/s/i-like tail, including a final high dot, is recoverable. It is recorded as one cancelled word. The subsequent live words read On a vu que. The separate small oval after On is a, not a full stop.
The phrase is de codim 1. The abbreviation codim has no detached final stop. The number 1 has a hooked upper start, upright and short basal return. No trailing punctuation is visible.

The complete phrase reads l'image inverse du diviseur. The beginning of inverse has a short i with a detached upper dot, followed by only low letters; there are no p/q descenders to justify a longer replacement word. image has a long g return. diviseur has two dotted i forms and low s/e/u/r ending. No terminal punctuation.

la fonction f is complete in the box. The article has a tall loop and small final bowl; fonction has the long first f, a tall crossed t and high i dot. The separate variable f has its own long descending loop. A clipped following d-like letter at the right belongs to adjacent text and is excluded.

The full line reads definie/définie si g >= 1 ou si S de dim 1 followed by three separate suspension points and a closing parenthesis. No distinct acute is securely visible over the first e, so the unaccented form is preferred locally. The comparison has an angle and a separate lower line, supporting geq. Both numerals 1 are retained as written. No est or abbreviation stop is supplied after dim, and no mathematical assertion was checked.

The phrase favors de tantot/tantôt, followed by a hooked comma. The second word has three tall t-like strokes: the initial stem, a medial crossed stem, and a final looped/crossed stem. Between them lie low a/n-like traces and a small dark o-like bowl. The tiny upper/left stroke near the o may be an accent or a connected return; no independent circumflex is secure, so tantot is preferred with tantôt retained. This is a visual reading, without expanding the reference.
Upper handwritten page number 46: angular open 4 and a long-arched 6 with a lower loop.
Lower-margin folio 92: looped 9 with a descending tail and a distinct 2 with a low horizontal base.

en fait le is followed by mu equals mu with a low alpha. The first mu has a descending left stem and short right shoulder; the second has the same form at greater size. The small alpha has a loop and a rightward tail, not the angular numeral 2. Two short equal bars are clear. The cropped upper descender belongs to the preceding line and is excluded.
